questions.question: In the context of Alkynes, what is the major organic product when 1-Butyne (CH₃CH₂-C≡C-H) reacts under the following conditions: 1. NaNH₂, liq. NH₃  2. CH₃CH₂Br?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Acetylide carbanion nucleophile displaces bromide from ethyl bromide via SN2 to elongate the carbon chain. The correct major product is '3-Hexyne (CH₃CH₂-C≡C-CH₂CH₃) + NaBr'.

questions.question: In the context of Alkynes, what is the major organic product when 1-Pentyne reacts under the following conditions: H₂O, H₂SO₄, HgSO₄ catalyst?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Markovnikov hydration yields an enol intermediate that rapidly tautomerizes to the methyl ketone. The correct major product is '2-Pentanone [CH₃-CO-CH₂CH₂CH₃]'.

questions.question: In the context of Alkynes, what is the major organic product when 1-Pentyne reacts under the following conditions: 1. (Sia)₂BH  2. H₂O₂, NaOH?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Sterically hindered dialkylborane adds anti-Markovnikov; alkaline oxidation yields the aldehyde via enol. The correct major product is 'Pentanal [CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CHO]'.

questions.question: In the context of Alkynes, what is the major organic product when 2-Butyne (CH₃-C≡C-CH₃) reacts under the following conditions: H₂ / Lindlar Catalyst (Pd/CaCO₃/PbO)?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Poisoned palladium catalyst allows syn addition of one equivalent of H₂ without overreduction to butane. The correct major product is 'cis-2-Butene [(Z)-2-Butene]'.

questions.topic: Dissolving Metal Trans Reduction of Alkyne
questions.question: In the context of Alkynes, what is the major organic product when 2-Butyne reacts under the following conditions: Na metal / liq. NH₃, -78°C?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Stepwise single-electron transfers and trans-radical anion intermediates yield the thermodynamically stable trans-alkene. The correct major product is 'trans-2-Butene [(E)-2-Butene]'.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert 1-Pentyne into Pentane in Alkynes?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation '1-Pentyne' → 'Pentane' specifically requires 'Excess H₂ / Pt(s) catalyst'. Mechanistic basis: Unpoisoned platinum catalyst completely reduces alkynes to saturated alkanes.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert Propyne (CH₃-C≡C-H) into 2,2-Dibromopropane [CH₃-CBr₂-CH₃] in Alkynes?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation 'Propyne (CH₃-C≡C-H)' → '2,2-Dibromopropane [CH₃-CBr₂-CH₃]' specifically requires 'Excess HBr(g)'. Mechanistic basis: Two sequential Markovnikov hydrohalogenations place both bromine atoms on C2 via resonance-stabilized halo-carbocations.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert 2-Butyne into 2,2,3,3-Tetrabromobutane in Alkynes?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation '2-Butyne' → '2,2,3,3-Tetrabromobutane' specifically requires 'Excess Br₂ in CCl₄'. Mechanistic basis: Electrophilic addition of two equivalents of bromine across the triple bond yields a vicinal tetrahaloalkane.

questions.question: Which starting material yields 'Acetic acid (CH₃COOH) + Propanoic acid (CH₃CH₂COOH)' when treated with '1. O₃, -78°C  2. H₂O workup' according to the principles of Alkynes?
